serpGaps: No ranking page ties the ROI model to a real, published build price. Ours uses the hub range ($60,000-$180,000, 8-16 weeks) as the cost input and links to it, so the reader gets a usable number instead of 'it depends'.

Competitors lead with headline multiples (671%, 5-10x, 6x faster) that trace to no primary source. We use one transparent formula, labelled assumptions and a low/expected/high range, and say which famous numbers to drop from a deck and why.

Nobody shows how to measure the baseline in 2-4 weeks before the build (time sampling, duplicate-component count from a UI inventory, UI bug tickets). Smashing and figr assume you already know 'time saved'.
Upkeep and adoption are an afterthought in most posts. We put upkeep, migration and adoption support in the cost stack and show how a slow adoption curve moves the payback month.

No page says when ROI is negative (1 product, 1-2 designers, stable UI) and what to buy instead (UI kit plus tokens). That honesty is our differentiator and links to the hub's 'Design system vs UI kit' section.
No downloadable or copyable one-page business case. We give the structure as an image plus 'Show as text' so readers can paste it into a doc.
Post-launch proof is vague. We name the instruments: Figma library analytics (component inserts and detaches), Storybook/Chromatic coverage, UI bug labels, time per screen.

outline.h2: What does design system ROI actually measure?
outline.answerHint: **Design system ROI compares the hours a shared library saves your designers and engineers with what the system costs to build and keep alive, over a set horizon.** Formula: (gain - cost) / cost x 100, gain = hours saved x loaded hourly cost.
points: Define gain (hours saved on UI design, build, QA and rework) and cost (build + upkeep + adoption support).

Pick a horizon: Smashing Magazine's model (Speicher and Baena Wehrmann, 2022) assumes a design system is useful for about 5 years before a major revamp. Cite it; do not reproduce their formula constants or worked example.
Say what stays outside the dollar figure and gets reported next to it: brand consistency, accessibility risk avoided, onboarding speed for new hires.
Link UP to the hub early: 'our design system services' -> /services/design-system-services/.

outline.h2: Which 5 inputs does the calculation need?
outline.answerHint: **You need 5 inputs: baseline UI hours, loaded hourly cost, expected share of time saved, build cost and annual upkeep.**
points: Baseline UI hours per sprint per team (design, front-end build, UI QA, rework).

Loaded hourly cost: start from BLS median pay for software developers and for web developers and digital designers, then add benefits using the BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation release. Cite exact figures and year from the BLS pages; do not use blog salary numbers.

Share of time saved as a range (low / expected / high), not one number. The only checkable public data point: Sparkbox timed 8 developers building a form page from scratch (4.2 hours) vs with IBM's Carbon Design System (2-hour median), about 47% faster. Present it as one small test of a mature system, an upper bound for early months, not a benchmark.

Build cost: agency fee plus your own engineers' time pairing on coded components. Link to /services/design-system-services/#how-much-does-a-design-system-cost for the price; do not restate the 4 price factors.
Annual upkeep: owner time (a fraction of a designer and an engineer), tooling licences, release work. Do not invent a percentage; tell the reader to estimate owner hours explicitly.

outline.h2: How do you measure a baseline before the build?
outline.answerHint: **Measure a baseline in 2-4 weeks with 3 cheap signals: time per screen, duplicate components and UI bug tickets.**
points: Time sampling: ask 3-5 designers and engineers to log hours on new screens and UI fixes for 2 sprints.

Duplicate count from a UI inventory: screenshots grouped by component (button styles, colour values, spacing values). This is step 1 of the hub process; deep link /services/design-system-services/#how-does-the-design-system-process-work.
UI bug and inconsistency tickets labelled in Jira/Linear over the last quarter.
Natural invitation: the UI inventory is the first deliverable of our engagement, so a team that buys the build gets its baseline as a by-product.

outline.h2: Worked example: payback for a 3-team SaaS product
outline.answerHint: **In this illustrative model, a 3-team product pays back a mid-range design system in month N.** (Writer computes N from the stated assumptions; every number is labelled as an assumption, not a result.)
points: Assumptions table (image + 'Show as text'): team size, sprint UI hours, loaded cost from BLS, build price chosen from inside the hub range, upkeep hours, savings ramp (for example 0% during build, rising to the expected rate by month 12).
Show the low / expected / high scenarios and the payback month for each.
State plainly: this is a model with invented inputs for illustration, not a client result. No client names (no case study on this site covers a design system).
Break-even curve visual: cumulative cost vs cumulative savings.

outline.h2: Which costs do most ROI models leave out?
outline.answerHint: **Most models leave out 5 costs: upkeep, migration of existing screens, adoption support, tooling and the productivity dip during the build.**
points: Migration: existing screens move to the new components over months; the hub FAQ says replacement happens screen by screen without a full redesign.
Adoption support: office hours, training workshops (hub process includes 2 workshops at rollout), contribution reviews.
Tooling: Figma organisation/enterprise seats for library analytics, Zeroheight, Chromatic. Writer must check current pricing pages or omit prices.
Productivity dip: teams slow down while the library is being built (Smashing model calls this out).

Ongoing maintenance options: in-house owner vs embedded team. One cross-hub link allowed here: /services/ux-consulting-services/ for embedded teams; do not restate its price beyond what the design-system hub cost section says.

outline.h2: When does a design system never pay back?
outline.answerHint: **A design system never pays back when 1 small team builds 1 stable product: the upkeep outruns the hours saved.** Buy a UI kit and tokens instead.
points: Use the hub's threshold wording: a full design system fits when 2 or more teams build on the same product; 1 product and 1-2 designers need a UI kit and tokens first. Link /services/design-system-services/#design-system-vs-ui-kit.
Other negative cases: product being sunset, rebrand planned with no time to tokenise, no engineer willing to own the coded library (Figma-only system = little build-time saving).
Decision tree visual: teams / products / platforms / planned rebrand -> UI kit, design system now, or wait.
Honest framing builds trust; end with 'if 2+ of these signals are true, the model is worth running'.

outline.h2: How do you turn the numbers into a one-page business case?
outline.answerHint: **A one-page business case has 6 blocks: the problem in hours, the ask, the payback range, the risks, the metrics you will report and the decision date.**
points: Tailor the headline per approver: CFO (payback month, cash out), CTO/VP Engineering (front-end hours, UI bugs), CPO (time to ship features, consistency across products).
Risks section: low adoption, scope creep in component count, owner leaving.
Put the low scenario first; finance trusts the conservative number.
Image of the one-pager + 'Show as text' version readers can paste.

outline.h2: Which metrics prove the ROI after launch?
outline.answerHint: **4 metrics prove the ROI after launch: adoption rate, component reuse rate, time per new screen and UI bug count.**
points: Adoption and detaches: Figma library analytics shows component inserts and detaches per team (writer: verify which Figma plans include library analytics on figma.com help pages).
Coded adoption: share of front-end screens importing library components; Storybook stories and Chromatic visual tests per component.
Time per new screen and UI bug tickets: re-run the baseline method at months 3, 6 and 12.
Report quarterly against the business case; this is part of design system governance (link hub governance wording, no new link needed if hub already linked twice).

outline.h2: What should you bring to a design system scoping call?
outline.answerHint: **Bring 4 facts to a scoping call: products and platforms in scope, number of brands or themes, your front-end stack and your baseline hours.**
points: These map to the hub's price drivers, so the quote lands inside the published $60,000-$180,000 range quickly. Link the cost section once (second hub link near the end).
Lead angle lives here: 'Book a free consultation with your baseline sheet and we will scope the build against it.' Do not promise a turnaround time or a free ROI report (not confirmed on the site).
Keep this section lean: BOFU, no extra links that pull away from the CTA.

faqs.q: Is a design system worth it for a small team?
faqs.a: No, not for 1 product with 1-2 designers. Start with a UI kit and design tokens; move to a design system when 2 or more teams build on the same product (hub wording).

faqs.q: How long does a design system take to pay back?
faqs.a: It depends on team size and adoption speed; the build alone takes 8-16 weeks before savings start. Run the low/expected/high model from this post rather than trusting a generic payback figure.

faqs.q: Can you estimate design system ROI without a baseline?
faqs.a: Yes, roughly: reconstruct UI hours from past tickets and pull-request history. Label it as an estimate and start real time sampling before the build begins.

faqs.q: Does a design system increase revenue?
faqs.a: No, not directly. It saves time and reduces UI defects; revenue effects come through faster releases and should be reported next to the ROI, not inside it.

faqs.q: Should accessibility count in design system ROI?
faqs.a: Yes, as risk avoided: components that hold WCAG 2.2 contrast and focus rules stop the same fix from repeating on every screen. Report it as fewer accessibility tickets rather than an invented dollar figure.

notes: CANNIBALISATION: the hub owns 'How much does a design system cost?' (price, 4 price factors, example tiers) and 'What are the benefits of a design system?' (4 benefits). Do not restate either: link the cost section and do not write a benefits list. The hub owns 'Should a startup build a design system?' and 'How long does a design system take?' FAQs: our FAQs are worded differently (worth it for a small team, payback time) and must answer from the ROI angle. No page on the site uses ROI/payback as a keyword; home.ts only mentions an 'ROI' calculator in the lead magnet and 'ROI-focused engagements' heading.

SITE-FACT CONFLICT 1 (flag for orchestrator): team threshold. Hub FAQ says a full design system fits 'when 2 or more teams build on the same product'; content/industries/startups.json says it 'pays off at Series B, when 3 or more squads ship in parallel'. The post uses the hub wording (2+ teams) only.

SITE-FACT CONFLICT 2: price label. Hub prices the design system alone at $60,000-$180,000; content/home.ts labels the same range 'Full design & design system' (end-to-end design plus system, 3-6 designers), and the saas hub calls it 'a full design and design system engagement'. Post says only 'design system engagement $60,000-$180,000, 8-16 weeks' via the hub link; do not state a team size.

SITE-FACT CONFLICT 3: terminology. ui-ux-design-services-for-startups sells a 'starter design system' (tokens + 20-30 core components) inside the $25,000-$60,000 sprint, while this hub calls that scope a UI kit ('Part of a $25,000-$60,000 design sprint') and puts a 25-30 component single-brand system near $60,000. Post uses 'UI kit and tokens' for the small-team option.

No case study in content/case-studies/ mentions a design system, component library or tokens: no DOWN link, no client names, no client results. The worked example must be labelled as illustrative with invented inputs.

DO NOT USE (unsourced or vendor-only claims seen in competitor snippets): Forrester '671% ROI'; McKinsey '20-30% savings'; '22% faster time to market'; '300-600% annual ROI, payback in 2-4 months'; '10-15x first year / 35-50x over 3 years'; '5-10x return'; Edana 'sprints up to 33% faster, UI tickets down 40-60%'; lollypop '6 weeks to 1 week' anecdote; Boundev '$47,300 design debt per team'; designprotocol '$150K-250K build, $50K-80K upkeep' (also contradicts the hub price); Supernova '$650,000 vs $97,600' (vendor comparison); '1 systems designer : 60 consumers' panel remark.

Originality: figr, lollypop, appstudio and supernova all open with headline multiples and a benefits list. Our order is definition -> inputs -> baseline -> worked example -> missed costs -> negative case -> one-pager -> post-launch metrics -> scoping. Do not paraphrase their 'speed, cost, quality, brand' pillars or lollypop's 'velocity, quality, alignment' framing.
Banned-word watch: the topic invites 'leverage' and 'seamless'; both are banned. Write 'use' and name the actual handoff.
Hub banking suggestion for the orchestrator: add one sentence to the hub's benefits or cost section linking 'design system ROI' to /blog/design-system-roi/ after publish.
